root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the first SHT_GROUP member section number is accepted and used as an index, `read_gs_section_group()` must enforce the strict upper-bound check `gseca < ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count`.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing path, the first decoded group member is `gseca == 4` while `ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4`, so the vulnerable `>` test treats the one-too-large equality case as in range. The fixed build changes this guard to reject equality before pointer formation, and the nearby valid boundary case reaches the protected dereference only when the strict inequality holds.

nodes.state: For the witnessed first group member, `targpsh = ep->f_shdr + gseca` computes `targpsh` equal to `ep->f_shdr + ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count`, i.e. a one-past-end `generic_shdr *`.
The first-group-member sink dereferences that same `targpsh` in `if (targpsh->gh_section_group_number)`, producing the AddressSanitizer-reported heap out-of-bounds read.

edges.relation: Because the strict upper-bound conjunct is missing, the same first-member `gseca` accepted by the guard is carried unchanged into `targpsh = ep->f_shdr + gseca`.
The one-past-end `targpsh` formed for the first group member is the exact pointer dereferenced at `targpsh->gh_section_group_number` on the crashing path.
